name: rsa-fermat
note: The Handbook of Applied Cryptography Example 8.4 publishes n=6012707, e=3674911, ciphertext c=3650502, and plaintext m=5234673. Its factors and private exponent are printed here only as expected outputs. The recovery test supplies n,e,c and the search budget, not p,q,d. Fermat checks a=2453 and a=2454, recovering p=2357 and q=2551 on its second square check, then computes d=422191 and decrypts m. The hash covers exactly three recovered big-endian bytes 4f df f1, not the decimal or hexadecimal text. Binary fields omit language plaintext/ciphertext fields so the text-only neural router does not consume this vector. This published artificially small textbook RSA example is not a general RSA break, padding attack, live-target attack, or unresolved historical decipherment.
